text.p: Poland's prime minister dismissed police chief Jerzy Stanczyk from his post on Friday, the national police spokesman said.
Stanczyk, who in March 1995 became Poland's fourth police chief since the 1989 fall of communism, announced last month that he planned to resign.
"The premier removed him today from his post," spokesman Andrzej Przemyski said.
PAP news agency quoted Intrior Minister Leszek Miller as saying Stanczyk would be replaced by his deputy Marek Papala.
The news agency said Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz also dismissed the head of the border guard service, Jan Wojcieszczuk, who was replaced by Andrzej Anklewicz.
Last year Stanczyk suffered a personal tragedy when his daughter died after being found unconscious with head wounds in a street near her home in the German city of Hamburg.

During Stanczyk's time at the helm, the government claimed successes in combating several kinds of crime, including car theft, assault and burglary -- all of which had grown since the collapse of the old communist order.
